answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. Think of that stake as a mesa: broad, visible, and expensive to climb onto. One honest agent pays once, but an attacker launching a comet swarm of fake identities must pay the stake for each one, like crossing a dune field where every dune costs real money. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its reputation burned, so fakes become a money-losing strategy instead of a free one.
